entities.name: PMID:25078447
observations: In MOG35–55/CFA-induced EAE, daily IVIG at 1 g/kg nearly prevented disease in wild-type mice but not IL-11 receptor alpha-deficient mice.

The study concluded that optimal IVIG attenuation of EAE requires an intact IL-11 receptor; receptor-deficient mice showed only initial protection and later developed EAE with failed Th17 suppression.

entities.name: Experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis
observations: In female C57BL/6J mice immunized with MOG35–55/CFA, daily high-dose IVIG beginning at induction nearly prevented clinical EAE in wild-type mice, with disease in 10% versus 100% of PBS controls.

entities.name: IL11RA
observations: IL-11 receptor alpha deficiency allowed only transient/initial IVIG protection; knockout mice subsequently developed EAE at incidence and severity similar to untreated knockout controls.
IVIG failed to suppress myelin-reactive Th17 cytokine production in IL-11Rα-deficient mice, unlike in wild-type mice.

entities.name: IVIG-IL11-EAE mechanism
observations: IVIG induced a greater than 1,000-fold circulating IL-11 surge, and IL-11 directly inhibited IL-17 production ex vivo, supporting IL-11 as an immune effector of IVIG-mediated prevention of Th17-driven EAE.
